# OpenMuscle

> OpenMuscle is an open-source, open-hardware project that builds affordable forearm pressure-myography (force myography) wearables and publishes labeled datasets for researchers in human-machine interfaces, prosthetic sensing and VR interfaces. The prediction targets are continuous finger flexion and extension, per-frame regression targets rather than gesture classes. The FlexGrid V4 band reads a 15x4 grid of 60 Velostat pressure cells with an ESP32-S3 at 17 to 19 Hz over Wi-Fi UDP, plus a 6-axis IMU. Ground-truth labels come from Meta Quest hand tracking (used with V4) or the LASK5 handheld labeler (recorded on the earlier V3 band; no V4 recording is LASK5-labeled). Hardware is CERN-OHL-S-2.0, software is MIT, and the dataset is CC BY 4.0.

OpenMuscle is early-stage research, not a finished product. The headline result from the paper is a generalization ladder for finger-flexion error (MAE, fraction of full curl): 0.043 with a random split, 0.110 with a temporal split, 0.24 on average (0.16 and 0.33 for the two wearers) when the band is re-donned in a new session, and 0.27 across wearers. Please cite the paper when using the data or results (see the research page).

## Site pages

- [Home](https://openmuscle.org/): What OpenMuscle is, a replay of real finger-prediction data, and the main repositories.
- [Technology](https://openmuscle.org/technology/): How pressure myography plus machine learning predicts fingers, devices compared, methodology.
- [Robotics](https://openmuscle.org/robotics/): Using human hand demonstrations from the band plus VR or HID labels as training data for robot hands.
- [Research and data](https://openmuscle.org/research/): The dataset, the paper, baseline results, and how to cite.
- [Repositories](https://openmuscle.org/repositories/): Every OpenMuscle GitHub repository with its license.
- [Get involved](https://openmuscle.org/get-involved/): Ways to test hardware, write code, and contribute data.
- [About](https://openmuscle.org/about/): Origin story, mission, project timeline and licenses.
- [Visual timeline](https://openmuscle.org/visual-timeline/): Photo timeline of the prototypes from 2022 to the FlexGrid flexible PCB.

## Dataset and paper

- [OpenMuscle FMG dataset on Hugging Face](https://huggingface.co/datasets/openmuscle/openmuscle-fmg): The dataset as Parquet files with a dataset card and the Dataset Viewer. 75 captures in four configs from two wearers, CC BY 4.0. DOI: [10.57967/hf/11416](https://doi.org/10.57967/hf/11416).
- [OpenMuscle-Dataset](https://github.com/Open-Muscle/OpenMuscle-Dataset): The raw drop on GitHub: capture sessions as plain text and CSV, CC BY 4.0.
- [Technical report v0.2, online](https://openmuscle.org/research/paper/): The full report as an HTML page, same text as the PDF, with figures and tables.
- [Technical report v0.2, PDF](https://openmuscle.org/papers/openmuscle-fmg-dataset-v0.2.pdf): The same report as a PDF.
- [Paper draft (Markdown)](https://github.com/Open-Muscle/OpenMuscle-Software/blob/main/analysis/paper/paper.md): Forearm force-myography with VR hand-tracking ground truth: dataset and honest baselines.
- [Paper analysis code](https://github.com/Open-Muscle/OpenMuscle-Software/tree/main/analysis/paper): Scripts that regenerate every number and figure in the paper from the raw captures.
- [How to cite](https://openmuscle.org/research/#cite): BibTeX and plain-text citation for the paper.

## GitHub repositories

- [OpenMuscle-Hub](https://github.com/Open-Muscle/OpenMuscle-Hub): Central hub and roadmap linking all repositories.
- [OpenMuscle-FlexGrid](https://github.com/Open-Muscle/OpenMuscle-FlexGrid): KiCad designs for the 60-sensor flexible band and rigid ESP32-S3 board (CERN-OHL-S-2.0).
- [FlexGridV4-Firmware](https://github.com/Open-Muscle/FlexGridV4-Firmware): MicroPython firmware for the FlexGrid V4 band (MIT).
- [OpenMuscle-LASK5](https://github.com/Open-Muscle/OpenMuscle-LASK5): Hardware for the LASK5 handheld finger-position labeler (CERN-OHL-S-2.0).
- [LASK5-Firmware](https://github.com/Open-Muscle/LASK5-Firmware): MicroPython firmware for the LASK5 labeler (MIT).
- [OpenMuscle-Software](https://github.com/Open-Muscle/OpenMuscle-Software): The OpenMuscle Studio PC app for capture, training and live prediction, plus the paper analysis (MIT).
- [OpenMuscle-AR](https://github.com/Open-Muscle/OpenMuscle-AR): WebXR client that streams Meta Quest hand tracking as labels (MIT).
- [OpenMuscle-Library](https://github.com/Open-Muscle/OpenMuscle-Library): Shared KiCad symbols, footprints and CAD parts.
- [OpenMuscle-Band](https://github.com/Open-Muscle/OpenMuscle-Band): The original 12-sensor OM-12 armband, a legacy design.

## Docs

- [Getting started](https://github.com/Open-Muscle/OpenMuscle-Software/blob/main/docs/getting-started.md): Install the app, connect the band to Wi-Fi, record, train and predict.
- [FlexGrid V4 band reference](https://github.com/Open-Muscle/FlexGridV4-Firmware/blob/main/docs/device-reference.md): Buttons, light patterns and screens of the band.
- [Troubleshooting](https://github.com/Open-Muscle/OpenMuscle-Software/blob/main/docs/troubleshooting.md): What to check when the band is not found or recording will not start.
- [Roadmap](https://github.com/Open-Muscle/OpenMuscle-Hub/blob/main/ROADMAP.md): Near-term milestones and long-term plans.
- [Contributing guide](https://github.com/Open-Muscle/.github/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md): How to contribute to any repository.
